Plot data as a pirate plot (RDI: raw data, descriptives, inferences)

Source: R/mypirate.R
pirateye.Rd

Makes a plot that shows the raw data points, a violin (the distribution), the mean, and error bars for the mean, for the conditions of an experiment. By default it draws all of those things, but you can turn on and off each element (dots, violin, bars, line, error_bars) and change the layout. Plots are saved as a pdf in outp, and returned as a ggplot that you can customise further. mypirate is an older name for the same function.

Usage

pirateye(
  data,
  colour_condition = NULL,
  x_condition = "variable",
  facet_condition = NULL,
  facet_scales = "fixed",
  facet_row = NULL,
  pid_average = F,
  norm_pid = "no",
  dv,
  reorder = "no",
  pid = "pid",
  dodgewidth = 0.8,
  plot_condition = NULL,
  cond = NULL,
  cond2 = NULL,
  facetby = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  xlim = NULL,
  w = NULL,
  h = 6,
  title = NULL,
  outp = "analysis",
  cols = NULL,
  pred_line = F,
  error_bar_data = NULL,
  ypercent = F,
  x_axis = NULL,
  y_axis = NULL,
  error_dim = F,
  error_dim_value = 0,
  pred = NULL,
  pred_means = NULL,
  pred_bar = T,
  xlabs = NULL,
  xlabpos = 0.7,
  col_pc_change = F,
  error_data = NULL,
  cflip = F,
  norm = F,
  norm_iq = F,
  norm_by = "none",
  norm_scale = "z",
  bars = F,
  violin = T,
  dots = T,
  splitV = F,
  svw = 1,
  dot_h_jitter = 0,
  line = F,
  error_bars = T,
  useall = F,
  legend = T,
  title_overide = F,
  combine_plots = list(),
  combine_position = "right",
  elementinc = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  saveoutdata = F,
  display_values = F,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or data.table (converted to a data.table in place).

colour_condition

Name of the column to split by colour.

x_condition

Name of the column for the x axis. If not given, the colour condition is used.

facet_condition

Name of the column that makes separate panels.

facet_scales

Scales for the panels: "fixed" (the same), "free" or "free_y" etc. (see ggplot2::facet_wrap).

facet_row

Number of rows of panels.

pid_average

Average each participant's dv over the conditions, before plotting?

dv

Name of the column to plot, or a vector of names of columns.

reorder

"increasing" or "decreasing" to put the conditions in order of their means. Default "no".

pid

Name of the column that identifies participants. Default "pid".

dodgewidth

How far apart to put the colour conditions within each x position.

plot_condition

A vector of up to three condition names, used instead of colour_condition, x_condition and facet_condition (in that order).

cond, cond2, facetby

Old names for x_condition, colour_condition and facet_condition.

ylim

Limits for the y axis, as a vector of two numbers.

xlim

Limits for the x axis.

w

Width of the saved plot in inches. By default this is chosen from the number of conditions.

h

Height of the saved plot in inches.

title

Title of the plot.

outp

Name of the folder for saving the plot as a pdf (it is created if needed). Set to NULL or "" to not save.

cols

The colours to use: a vector of colours, or a named vector matching condition levels to colours. If the condition levels are themselves colour names, those are used.

pred_line

Draw pred_means as a line rather than as bars?

error_bar_data

A table of ymin and ymax values to use for the error bars, instead of calculating standard errors from the data, with the same condition columns as the plot. Used by plot_model().

ypercent

Show the y axis as a percentage?

x_axis

Label for the x axis (default is the condition name).

y_axis

Label for the y axis (default is the dv name).

error_dim

Fade out the data for the conditions whose mean (with SE) excludes error_dim_value.

error_dim_value

The value used by error_dim.

pred

Optional table of predicted data (eg samples from a model), shown as violins.

pred_means

Optional table of predicted means, shown as bars or lines.

pred_bar

Draw pred_means as bars? Default TRUE.

xlabs

A table of labels to show above the x axis, such as post hoc p-values. It needs a column called lab, and the same x condition column as the plot.

xlabpos

How high up the labels in xlabs go, as a proportion of the height of the plot.

col_pc_change

Calculate the percentage change from the first to the second colour condition and show it along the x axis.

error_data

Not currently used.

cflip

Flip the plot so that the x axis is vertical?

norm, norm_pid, norm_iq

Old arguments for normalising. Use norm_by and norm_scale instead.

norm_by

Normalise by "pid" or by "dv", or "none" (the default).

norm_scale

"z" (the default) for z scores, or "iq" for a scale with a mean of 100 and an SD of 15.

bars

Show means as bars?

violin

Show violins of the distributions?

dots

Show a point for each data point?

splitV

Draw a split violin (half for each colour) when there are two colour conditions.

svw

Width of the split violins.

dot_h_jitter

Amount of vertical jitter for the dots.

line

Join the means with lines?

error_bars

Show error bars (standard errors)?

useall

Plot all rows, ignoring any use column.

legend

Show the legend? It is hidden when colour and x axis show the same condition.

title_overide

If TRUE, the file name is made from the title alone rather than also adding the dv and conditions.

combine_plots

A list of other plots to put together with this one (using cowplot).

combine_position

Where to put the combined plots: "right" or "under".

elementinc

An extra ggplot element (eg a theme) added to the plot early on.

type

Shortcut: "m" shows only the means and error bars, "b" shows just bars and error bars.

saveoutdata

Also save the data used for the plot, as a .csv file.

display_values

Write the mean values on the plot?

...

Not currently used.

Value

A ggplot object (or a combined cowplot figure if combine_plots is used).

Details

Specifying the conditions

  • x_condition is the column shown along the x axis, colour_condition splits by colour, and facet_condition makes a separate panel for each level. plot_condition is a shortcut where you give a vector of up to three names, in the order colour, x, facet.

  • If you give only colour_condition it is also used for the x axis.

  • dv is the column with the data to plot. If you give several columns, they are stacked into a column called variable, which you can use as a condition.

  • Data should be in long format, with a row for each observation (for example each trial), and a column identifying participants (pid). Set pid_average = TRUE to average each participant's data within conditions before plotting.

  • If the data has a column called use, only rows where use is 1 are plotted, unless you set useall = TRUE.

Normalising: norm_by = "dv" converts values to z scores for each of the dvs, so that you can compare them on one axis. norm_by = "pid" does that for each participant. Use norm_scale = "iq" for a scale with mean 100 and standard deviation 15 instead.

Saving: the file name is made from the title, the dv and the names of the conditions. Set outp = NULL to avoid saving a file.

Old arguments cond, cond2, facetby, norm, norm_iq, norm_pid are kept so that old code still works. Use x_condition, colour_condition, facet_condition, norm_by and norm_scale in new code.

See also

plot_model()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pirateye(data = iat_data, colour_condition = "congruency",
         x_condition = "firstblock", dv = "rt", outp = NULL)
# average over participants, with bars rather than violins
pirateye(iat_data, colour_condition = "congruency", x_condition = "firstblock",
         dv = "rt", pid_average = TRUE, violin = FALSE, bars = TRUE, outp = NULL)
} # }
